docs.title: Phinder
docs.text: Phinder is a Java application that uses the Phileas library to identify PII (Personally Identifiable Information) in text across a wide variety of file formats.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-format Support: Process Plain Text, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, CSV, RTF, Emails, Log files, and Images.
  • Recursive Processing: Scan entire directories and their subdirectories.
  • Customizable Policies: Use Phileas policies to define what PII to look for.
  • Risk Scoring: Rank files by how sensitive their PII is, not just how much of it there is, so the riskiest data gets remediated first.
  • Magnitude & Density Scoring: Calculate scores based on the types, counts, and concentration of PII found.
  • Reporting: Always generates HTML and JSON reports.
  • High Performance: Optimized for handling large files and millions of documents.

docs.title: How it Works
docs.text: Phinder extracts text from various file formats and uses Phileas's PlainTextFilterService to identify PII spans. It also checks file names for PII. Results are aggregated and can be exported as reports.

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
Phinder is a command-line application. Below is a list of all available options.

Option Long Option Description -i --input Required. The input file(s) or directories to scan. Repeat for multiple. -R --recursive Recursively traverse subdirectories if directories are provided. -p --policy Path to a custom Phileas policy (JSON file). --emit-policy Write a starter redaction policy covering the entity types found, to the given file. Emits PhiSQL for a .phisql file, otherwise JSON. -w --weights Path to custom PII weights (JSON file) used for the Magnitude Score. --severities Path to custom PII risk severities (JSON file) used for the Risk Score. --sort-by Order the per-file report sections by risk, magnitude, density, or name. (Default: risk) --min-risk Omit files scoring below this Risk Score from the per-file report sections. Aggregate totals still cover the whole scan. (Default: 0) --top How many files to list as candidates for redaction testing. (Default: 20) -l --log Enable the scan log using a MongoDB database. -s --skip-unchanged Skip scanning files that haven't changed since the last scan log. --clean Truncate the scan log database. --mongodb The MongoDB URI for the scan log and report history. --csv-delimiter Custom CSV delimiter character. (Default: ,) --csv-quote Custom CSV quote character. (Default: ") -h --help Show the help message and exit. -V --version Show the application version and exit.

docs.title: Scan multiple files
docs.text: java -jar phinder.jar -i file1.txt -i file2.docx

docs.title: Scan a directory recursively with custom weights
docs.text: java -jar phinder.jar -i my_docs/ -R -w weights.json

docs.title: Prioritize the riskiest files
docs.text: java -jar phinder.jar -i my_docs/ -R --sort-by risk --min-risk 50 --top 10

docs.title: Scan with custom risk severities
docs.text: java -jar phinder.jar -i my_docs/ -R --severities my-severities.json

docs.title: Generate a starter redaction policy from a scan
docs.text:
java -jar phinder.jar -i my_docs/ -R --emit-policy starter-policy.json

To get the policy as PhiSQL instead, use a .phisql extension:

java -jar phinder.jar -i my_docs/ -R --emit-policy starter-policy.phisql

docs.title: What is Phinder?
docs.text: Phinder is a command-line application that identifies Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in various file formats, such as PDF, Word, Excel, and more. It uses the Phileas library for PII detection.

docs.title: Which file formats are supported?
docs.text: Phinder supports a wide range of formats including: - Plain Text (.txt, .log) - Adobe PDF (.pdf) - Microsoft Word (.doc, .docx) - Microsoft Excel (.xls, .xlsx) - Microsoft PowerPoint (.ppt, .pptx) - Comma-Separated Values (.csv) - Rich Text Format (.rtf) - Email Messages (.eml, .msg) - Images (.png, .jpg, .tiff) via OCR

docs.title: How do I define what PII to look for?
docs.text: You can provide a Phileas policy file in JSON format using the -p or --policy option. This policy defines the types of PII (e.g., names, SSNs, credit card numbers) to detect.

docs.title: Can I scan entire directories?
docs.text: Yes, Phinder can scan a single file or an entire directory. Use the -R or --recursive flag to scan subdirectories as well.

docs.title: How does Phinder handle large files?
docs.text: Phinder is designed for high performance. Large log files are processed line-by-line to minimize memory usage, and other formats are handled efficiently using specialized processors.

docs.title: What are the Risk, Magnitude, and Density scores?
docs.text:
• Risk Score: How sensitive the PII in a document is. It combines the severity of each entity type, how many occurrences were found, and how confident the detector was, and is reported with a risk level from NONE to CRITICAL. Use it to decide what to remediate first. See Risk Scoring.
  • Magnitude Score: A weighted score representing the total amount of PII found in a document. You can customize the weights for different PII types.
  • Density Score: The ratio of PII findings to the total amount of text in the document.

docs.title: Why does a file with less PII sometimes have a higher Risk Score?
docs.text: Because the Risk Score measures sensitivity rather than volume. Two Social Security numbers outrank fifty city names. The Magnitude Score is the one that answers "how much PII is in here"; the two are calculated and configured independently, so tuning one does not move the other.

docs.title: Does the Risk Score tell me whether I am compliant?
docs.text: No. It is a prioritization aid built from the entity types a scan found. It does not know how a file is stored, who can read it, or whether the detections are correct: detection is probabilistic, so a scan may both miss PII and flag text that is not PII. Review the findings against your own data before acting on the ranking.

docs.title: How can I speed up subsequent scans?
docs.text: You can use the --log and --skip-unchanged options. Phinder will maintain a log (in a MongoDB database) of the files it has already scanned and their hashes. On subsequent runs, it will skip files that haven't changed. You must provide the MongoDB connection string via the PHINDER_MONGODB_URI environment variable.

docs.title: In what formats are the reports generated?
docs.text: Phinder always generates both HTML (.html) and JSON (.json) reports.

docs.title: How is OCR handled for images?
docs.text: Phinder uses Tesseract for OCR. You may need to set the TESSDATA_PREFIX environment variable to the directory containing your Tesseract language data files (e.g., eng.traineddata).

docs.title: Does Phinder require an internet connection?
docs.text: No, Phinder performs all PII detection locally using the Phileas library and does not send your data to any external services.

docs.title: Does Phinder redact the PII?
docs.text: No, Phinder is designed for identification and reporting of PII. If you need to redact or anonymize PII, consider using Philter.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Java 21 or higher
  • Maven 3.x
  • Tesseract OCR (optional, required for processing images)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Clone the repository and build the project using Maven:

mvn clean install

This will create a runnable shaded JAR in the target/ directory.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To scan a single text file:

java -jar target/phinder-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar -i input.txt

To scan a directory:

java -jar target/phinder-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar -i /path/to/my/files/

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: Phinder always generates an HTML and JSON report (report.html and report.json).

docs.title: Report Formats
docs.text: Format File Description HTML report.html A modern, visually attractive HTML report. JSON report.json A machine-readable JSON file.

docs.title: Generating a Report
docs.text: Reports are always generated at the end of a scan.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: java -jar phinder.jar -i input.txt

docs.title: Report Content
docs.text: Every report includes: 1. Report ID: A unique UUID for the scan. 2. Timestamp: The date and time the scan was completed. 3. Aggregate Risk Score and Risk Level: How sensitive the PII across all files is. See Risk Scoring. 4. Aggregate Magnitude Score: Total magnitude across all files. 5. Aggregate Density Score: Magnitude score divided by total word count across all files. 6. Aggregate PII Counts: Total number of occurrences for each PII type. 7. Files Skipped: The number of files skipped because they hadn't changed since the last scan. 8. PII Weights and Severities: The weights used for the Magnitude Score, and the severity used for each detected PII type in the Risk Score. 9. Best Candidates for Redaction Testing: A table of the highest-scoring files, capped by --top (HTML format only). 10. Per-file Details: For each file, the Risk Score and Risk Level, the Magnitude and Density Scores, and the counts of each PII type found.

docs.title: Ordering and Filtering
docs.text:
The per-file sections are ordered by Risk Score by default, so the files worth remediating first appear first. Use --sort-by risk|magnitude|density|name to change the ordering, --min-risk to leave low-risk files out, and --top to size the candidates table:

java -jar phinder.jar -i my_docs/ -R --sort-by risk --min-risk 50 --top 10

--min-risk changes which files are listed, not which files were scanned. Aggregate scores and counts always cover the whole scan, and the JSON report records both filesReported and filesScanned.

docs.title: Report History
docs.text:
If the --mongodb option is used, the report will also be stored in the specified MongoDB database.

java -jar target/phinder-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar -i src/test/resources/input.txt --mongodb "mongodb://localhost:27017/phinder"

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text:
Phinder identifies PII in both the file contents and the file name.

Category Extensions Notes Plain Text .txt, .md Markdown is supported. Documents .pdf, .docx, .doc, .rtf Spreadsheets .xlsx, .xls, .csv CSV delimiter and quoting can be customized. Presentations .pptx, .ppt Extracts from slides, notes, and comments. Email .eml, .msg Extracts subject, sender, and body. Logs .log Processed line-by-line for memory efficiency. Images .png, .jpg, .jpeg Requires Tesseract OCR installed.

Note

Processing images requires tesseract-ocr to be installed on your system.

docs.title: Processing Files
docs.text:
You can specify one or more files using the -i or --input option:

java -jar phinder.jar -i file1.txt -i file2.pdf

docs.title: Processing Directories
docs.text:
To process all supported files in a directory:

java -jar phinder.jar -i /path/to/directory

docs.title: Recursive Search
docs.text:
Use the -R or --recursive flag to traverse subdirectories:

java -jar phinder.jar -i /path/to/directory -R

docs.title: CSV Customization
docs.text:
When processing CSV files, you can specify the delimiter and quote character:

java -jar phinder.jar -i data.csv --csv-delimiter=";" --csv-quote="'"

docs.title: Generating a Starter Redaction Policy
docs.text:
Phinder can turn a scan into a starter Philter / Phileas redaction policy, so discovery and redaction become one workflow. Add --emit-policy with an output file:

java -jar phinder.jar -i my_docs/ -R --emit-policy starter-policy.json

The flow is scan, then policy, then apply:

  1. Scan. Phinder finds the entity types present across the inputs.
  2. Policy. It writes redaction-policy JSON that enables each detected type with a REDACT strategy. The output loads unchanged into Philter or Phileas. Use a .phisql file extension to get the policy as PhiSQL instead, which compiles to the same JSON. Types that need a supplied custom policy to detect (custom identifiers, sections, or PhEye name detection) are reported as skipped rather than guessed at.
  3. Apply. Use the policy with Philter or Phileas directly, or tune it first (change strategies, add conditions, ignore terms) and re-run.

This is a starting point to review, tune, and measure (for example with Philter Scope) before you rely on it. Redaction is probabilistic: it reduces how much sensitive data gets through, it does not catch every instance, and you are responsible for validating the policy against your own data.

docs.title: Large File Support
docs.text: Phinder is designed to handle very large files efficiently. Specifically, .log files are processed line-by-line to minimize heap usage.

docs.title: Scan Logging and Skipping
docs.text: To speed up subsequent scans, Phinder can maintain a log of scanned files and their xxHash64 hashes using a MongoDB database.

docs.title: MongoDB Configuration
docs.text:
To use the scan log, you must provide a MongoDB connection string via the PHINDER_MONGODB_URI environment variable:

export PHINDER_MONGODB_URI="mongodb://localhost:27017"

docs.title: Generating a Scan Log
docs.text:
By default, using --log or --skip-unchanged will enable the scan log using the MongoDB database specified in PHINDER_MONGODB_URI.

java -jar phinder.jar -i /path/to/data --log

docs.title: Skipping Unchanged Files
docs.text:
On the next run, use --skip-unchanged to skip any file that hasn't changed (based on its xxHash64 hash):

java -jar phinder.jar -i /path/to/data --skip-unchanged

Phinder will compare the file names and hash values in the MongoDB database to determine if a file can be skipped. The count of skipped files will be included in the reports.

When using the scan log, Phinder also stores a timestamped copy of the scan results in a reports collection in the MongoDB database. This allows for historical tracking of scan results.

docs.title: Cleaning the Scan Log
docs.text:
To clear the recorded hashes and paths from the scan log database, use the --clean option:

java -jar phinder.jar --clean

This will delete the entries in the scan log collections, forcing all files to be re-scanned on the next run with --skip-unchanged.

docs.title: Phileas Policy
docs.text: Phinder uses the Phileas library to perform PII detection. You can provide a custom Phileas policy in JSON format using the -p or --policy option.

docs.title: Example Policy
docs.text:
A policy defines which identifiers (PII types) to enable.

{
  "identifiers": {
    "emailAddress": {
      "emailAddressFilterStrategies": [
        {
          "strategy": "REDACT",
          "redaction": "[[EMAIL]]"
        }
      ]
    },
    "ssn": {
      "ssnFilterStrategies": [
        {
          "strategy": "REDACT",
          "redaction": "[[SSN]]"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Applying the Policy
docs.text:
java -jar phinder.jar -i input.txt -p my-policy.json

If no policy is provided, Phinder uses a default policy that looks for email addresses.

docs.title: Risk Scoring
docs.text: Phinder assigns a Risk Score to each file and to the scan as a whole, so you can decide what to remediate first. Unlike the Magnitude Score, which counts occurrences, the Risk Score accounts for how sensitive each entity type is. A file with two Social Security numbers ranks above a file with fifty city names, even though the second file has far more PII in it.

docs.title: Calculation
docs.text:
For each entity type found, Phinder multiplies three things and sums the result:

Risk Score = Sum over types of ( severity * count * confidenceFactor )
Term Meaning severity How damaging one leaked value of that type is. See the table below. count How many occurrences of that type were found. confidenceFactor 0.5 + (0.5 * average detection confidence), so a value between 0.5 and 1.0.

Confidence discounts a finding, it never erases it. A detector that is unsure still found something worth a look, so a zero-confidence hit counts half as much as a certain one rather than nothing at all.

docs.title: Risk Levels
docs.text:
Each score is reported alongside a band, so a report is readable without doing arithmetic:

Level Risk Score NONE 0 LOW Above 0 and below 10 MEDIUM 10 to below 50 HIGH 50 to below 250 CRITICAL 250 and above

docs.title: Default Severities
docs.text:
Severities are ordinal judgements about how much damage one leaked value does, not measurements. They are the starting point Phinder ships with so that a Social Security number does not rank alongside a city name out of the box. Tune them for your own data and threat model.

Severity Entity types 10.0 bank-routing-number, credit-card, drivers-license-number, iban-code, passport-number, ssn 8.0 bitcoin-address, medical-condition 5.0 email-address, id, person, pheye, phone-number, physician-name, street-address, vin 3.0 age, custom-dictionary, first-name, ip-address, surname 2.0 date, hospital, hospital-abbreviation, mac-address, phone-number-extension, tracking-number, zip-code 1.0 city, county, currency, other, section, state, state-abbreviation, url

An entity type that is not in this table, such as one produced by a custom identifier in your own policy, gets a severity of 1.0.

docs.title: Custom Severities
docs.text:
Pass a JSON object mapping entity types to severities with --severities. Types you do not name keep their default.

{
  "medical-condition": 10.0,
  "first-name": 5.0,
  "url": 0.5
}

java -jar phinder.jar -i documents/ -R --severities my-severities.json

The severities in effect for the types a scan found are written into report.json and the HTML report, so a report always records the scoring it was produced with.

docs.title: Sorting and Filtering
docs.text:
The per-file sections of a report are ordered by Risk Score by default. Change the ordering with --sort-by, drop low-risk files with --min-risk, and set how many files appear in the "Best Candidates for Redaction Testing" table with --top:

java -jar phinder.jar -i documents/ -R --sort-by risk --min-risk 50 --top 10

--min-risk changes which files are listed, not which files were scanned. The aggregate scores and counts always cover the whole scan, and report.json records both filesReported and filesScanned so the difference is never hidden.

docs.title: Risk Score and Magnitude Score
docs.text:
The two scores answer different questions and are calculated independently:

Magnitude Score Risk Score Question How much PII is in this file? How sensitive is the PII in this file? Per-type factor Weight, default 1.0 for every type Severity, from the table above Uses confidence No Yes Configured with --weights --severities

Because they are independent, a weights.json file tunes the Magnitude Score only and cannot move the Risk Score, and vice versa.

docs.title: What the Risk Score Is Not
docs.text: The Risk Score is a prioritization aid built from the entity types a scan found. It is not a measure of regulatory exposure or a compliance determination. It does not know how a file is stored, who can read it, how the values combine across records, or whether the detections are correct in the first place: detection is probabilistic, and a scan may both miss PII and report text that is not PII. Review the findings against your own data before acting on the ranking, and treat the score as a way to order your work rather than as a verdict on it.

docs.title: Magnitude Score Weights
docs.text:
Phinder calculates a Magnitude Score for each file and an aggregate score for the entire scan. By default, every PII occurrence has a weight of 1.0.

Note

The Magnitude Score measures how much PII a file holds, not how sensitive it is. To rank files by sensitivity instead, see Risk Scoring, which is calculated separately and configured separately. Weights tune the Magnitude Score only and do not affect the Risk Score.

docs.title: Custom Weights
docs.text: You can specify custom weights for different PII types using a weights.json file. This allows you to prioritize certain types of PII over others (e.g., a SSN might have a higher magnitude than an email address).

docs.title: weights.json Format
docs.text:
The file should be a JSON object mapping PII types (as identified by Phileas) to numeric weights.

{
  "email-address": 2.0,
  "ssn": 10.0,
  "phone-number": 5.0
}

docs.title: Using Weights
docs.text:
Specify the weights file with the -w or --weights option:

java -jar phinder.jar -i documents/ -w my-weights.json

docs.title: Calculation
docs.text: The Magnitude Score is calculated as: Sum(PII Type Count * PII Type Weight)

docs.title: Density Score
docs.text:
Phinder also calculates a Density Score, which is the Magnitude Score divided by the word count of the document: Density Score = Magnitude Score / Word Count

This score helps identify documents with a high concentration of PII relative to their size.

docs.title: Weights and Severities
docs.text:
Weights and severities look alike and are easy to confuse:

Weight Severity Feeds Magnitude Score, Density Score Risk Score Default 1.0 for every type Per type, from the built-in severity table Option --weights --severities

Setting one has no effect on the other, so you can tune each for what it measures.
